key_insight: CARM makes sequence-level RL masking cancellation-aware by averaging absolute token log-ratios, so opposing probability shifts cannot hide off-policy drift.
engineering_relevance: This gives LLM training pipelines a more robust way to control rollout-policy mismatch during post-training, especially for math reasoning and code generation.
method: Compute token log-ratios between sampled and training policies.
Average absolute log-ratios across the response to decide whether to accept or mask it.
Use a joint theoretical bound to control both out-of-band ratio frequency and average log-distance.
evidence_signal: On math benchmarks, CARM improves mean@16 by up to 3.13 points over geometric-mean masking, and on four code benchmarks it raises average pass@1 by 2.88 points over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Because it changes the masking criterion at the sequence level, performance may depend on threshold tuning and on how well the rollout and training engines are aligned.
paper_title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
